page: Microsoft Azure M416s_9_v3 is an ultra-dense, memory-optimized instance in the MSHighMemoryv3 family. It provides 416 dedicated vCPUs on an x86_64 Intel architecture and integrates 8,568.0 GB of RAM. This resource allocation establishes an extensive memory density of approximately 20.6 GB per core, serving compute jobs that must maintain massive working sets in system memory. The instance runs on Microsoft Hyper-V and contains zero hardware-accelerated GPUs.

Storage architecture on the M416s_9_v3 does not include bundled local or ephemeral disks. All persistent operational files, operating system installations, and data logging depend directly on external storage connectivity, such as Azure Premium Storage volumes. This architectural choice decouples persistent disk IOPS and throughput from host hardware, making input and output capacity reliant on network storage provisioning rather than fast local scratch disks.

Resource allocation focuses heavily on memory capacity relative to core count. The server is engineered specifically for hyper-scale enterprise software architectures, such as production SAP HANA platforms, large-scale relational database engines, complex data warehousing systems, and memory-bound transactional applications that demand enterprise-scale memory pools.
description: Microsoft Azure M416s_9_v3 is an ultra-high-capacity, memory-optimized instance from the MSHighMemoryv3 family. Powered by x86_64 Intel architecture, the server provides 416 dedicated vCPUs and 8,568.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a high resource density of 20.6 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes no GPU acceleration and does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating the use of remote storage such as Azure Premium Storage for all filesystem and paging operations. The hardware distribution prioritizes vast memory footprints and dedicated CPU execution rather than local I/O caching. Consequently, the M416s_9_v3 is intended for large-scale enterprise data operations, including massive in-memory databases like SAP HANA, high-demand data warehousing clusters, enterprise resource planning platforms, and large relational database instances requiring continuous in-memory processing.
